$comment: The interpolation findings both analyses give the files of the test project in this folder, copied verbatim from the user's interpolationtests project, where every form of A to C also writes query, text from the request, somewhere it does harm, and D_EveryPosition.kt writes every kind of value into every position, with what the editor must say above each line, as E_Interpolate.kt does for calls to interpolate: analyzeKotlin in editors/vscode/src/analyze.ts and Analyzer.analyzeKotlin in streamlord-analysis, each file on its own, with the const vals the workspace declares (constants) known, as the VS Code index and IntelliJ provide them. Only the interpolation codes are listed (kotlin-interpolation, unescaped-interpolation, unsafe-interpolation, interpolate-template, interpolate-holes), and missing-id and top-level-text must not appear in any file. Offsets count UTF-16 code units; line is for the reader. What IntelliJ adds with types is in the plugin's own InspectionTest.

Kotlin fills in ${query} before interpolate sees the markup, so interpolate neither escapes nor refuses it. It lands in data-on:click, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path. Put the value in a signal and reference it from the expression, or write the signal's name in the markup yourself.

Kotlin interpolates $count here, as the whole Datastar expression. Meant as a server value, only a number or a boolean is safe there; meant as the signal $count, make the whole literal $$"""...""" (Kotlin 2.2+), or escape as ${'$'}count.
